newsitem.title: CHINA: China coal market seen week throughout 1997.
newsitem.headline: China coal market seen week throughout 1997.

text.p: China's coal market is in a slump and is expected to stay there throughout 1997 as weakening demand and rising stocks compound price falls that began last year, the Business News said on Monday.
Even as output had fallen on a year-on-year basis, stocks remained high as Chinese consumers were increasingly choosy about the quality and type of coal they bought, it said.
Total 1996 coal output was 1.37 billion tonnes, the newspaper quoted official statistics as showing.
Chinese officials hoped to maintain that output level in 1997, but to reduce stocks by 45 million tonnes, it said.
China's total coal stocks had hit 200 million tonnes, with stock held by key state-owned coal mines at 35 million tonnes, much higher than the rational level, the newspaper said.
Sluggish production, especially in the machinery and electricity sectors, had cut demand for coal and seriously impacted the coal market, it quoted industry analysts as saying.
